title: Quarterly leverboard experiments — personal log
content:
Context:
This is my personal planning + tracking scratchpad for a compact set of 'leverboard' experiments I want to run across Q1–Q2. The idea: pick 3–4 small, measurable levers (prompt caching, batching config, model variant routing, cost-per-token profiling) and run short experiments to see which moves the needle on two personal KPIs: (A) reduce per-100k-token hosted cost by 12% and (B) improve P95 generation latency by 10% for the shipping chat route.

Why a personal log?
- I want a lightweight, iterated record (not the canonical team RFC).
- Capture raw observations, early signal numbers, and blockers so I can feed PRDs and demos later.
- Keep a weekly cadence of short retros and next actions.

Top-level OKRs I'm targeting (personal):
- OKR 1: Cost efficiency — "Reduce hosted token unit cost"
  - Target metric: 12% reduction in billed inference cost per 100k tokens on the test workload by end of Q2.
- OKR 2: Latency & UX — "Tighter P95 latency for chat route"
  - Target metric: 10% improvement in P95 generation latency (pinned to 1k-token window).
- OKR 3: Knowledge transfer — "Document 3 concrete ops playbooks"
  - Deliverables: playbook for smart-batching, KV-cache warmup, and model-routing fallback.

Hypotheses (short):
- H1: Enabling prefix-based KV caching for common prompt prefixes will reduce token compute by ~6–10% on repeated flows (notes: shipping welcome message + context).
- H2: Tightening the batching window (tradeoff: slightly higher latency for cold requests) combined with adaptive timeouts will improve throughput and net cost by ~8%.
- H3: Canary routing to a 3-bit quantized variant during low traffic windows will cut per-token GPU compute cost with <1% regression in model quality (measured by pass rate on 30 chosen eval prompts).
- H4: Adding a light-weight token-level early-stop heuristic for long outputs (for specific system messages) will shave tokens for 5% of calls.

Experiment inventory (short entries):
1) Prefix KV cache pilot
   - Start: 2026-01-15
   - Status: running (signal: early positive)
   - Quick description: capture top 20 prompt prefixes for chat onboarding flows, cache their KV states for 30s TTL, warm on subsequent requests.
   - Metrics to watch: cache-hit rate, tokens saved per 1k requests, median latency change, quality diffs on eval set.
   - Early signals (week 2): 18% hit rate on targeted flows, estimated 4.3% token savings. Quality delta: negligible on 200 sample checks.
   - Blockers: infra trace visibility for cross-pod cache hits; SRE flagged TTL amplification risk.
   - Next action: add a cheap tracing counter and add TTL jitter; draft playbook section.

2) Adaptive batching window tweak
   - Start: 2026-02-02
   - Status: paused (waiting on perf infra metric mapping)
   - Description: lower max batching latency from 25ms to 15ms for premium tier, try 10–25ms adaptive policy that tightens when concurrency low.
   - Hypothesis: higher per-batch token density with tiny latency tradeoff -> cost per token down.
   - Early signals: on local perf harness, batch size increased 1.4x for synthetic workload but end-to-end P95 increased ~6%.
   - Concerns: SLA implications; need product alignment for premium tier.
   - Next: sync with product-hosted-api on tier-level SLAs (todo: ping Mina).

3) Quantized fallback canary
   - Start: 2026-02-18
   - Status: design
   - Description: route 3% of low-priority traffic to a 3-bit quantized shim with automatic rollback if eval pass rate < 99%.
   - Metric: quality pass-rate on 30 eval prompts, per-token GPU seconds, cost delta.
   - Early design note: include same-tokenization and log-likelihood checks to detect silent failure modes.
   - Risks: regressions in named-entity stability, hallucination increase.

4) Early-stop heuristic for system responses
   - Start: 2026-02-25
   - Status: draft
   - Description: detect canonical system message tails (e.g., "Here are the steps:") and apply a token-stop clamp if next tokens are high-entropy and low-value.
   - Quick test: rule-based filter on 500 samples -> reduced tokens in 6.1% of cases, manual check showed 2/30 examples with truncated useful data.
   - Next: try soft-stop (punish but allow extension if user asks).

Weekly check-ins (personal):
- 2026-01-22: KV cache pilot looks promising. Need better observability and a safe TTL policy. Put draft config in personal branch.
- 2026-01-29: Short retrospective — caching helps for onboarding flows, but edge-case where user context changes mid-session. Note: TTL should be anchored to session id when present.
- 2026-02-12: Adaptive batching local sim encouraging; ask product about premium-tier latency budget.
- 2026-02-26: Canary quantization RFC drafted; shared with Mina for review.
- 2026-03-05: Consolidated learnings; start drafting the three short playbooks.

Retrospective notes (raw):
- What worked: small scoped experiments give quick signals; pairing with SRE early avoided noisy incidents.
- What didn't: I under-estimated observability needs — many metrics lived in separate dashboards. Need a unified perf slice for my experiments.
- Surprises: caching benefits are larger for chat flows with repeated templates vs freeform queries.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- TTL policy: session-anchored vs unbound short TTL (safety tradeoffs).
- SLA tolerance: what P95 increase is acceptable for premium-tier adaptive batching? Need product signoff.
- Eval coverage: is a 30-prompt eval for quantization too small? Propose 200 prompt suite with focused failure-case tags.

To-dos (ordered):
- [ ] Add a 1-line trace counter for cross-pod cache hits (INF-2981) — due 2026-03-10 — assigned: me.
- [ ] Sync with Mina on premium-tier latency deck — schedule 15m sync.
- [ ] Draft playbook: "KV cache pilot — ops checklist" — first draft by 2026-03-12.
- [ ] Expand quantization eval set to 200 prompts and automates scoring — ask research for support.

Notes to self (short, informal):
- Keep experiments <= 4 weeks each unless signal is ambiguous.
- Record failures as lessons (not just wins) — this doc is the canonical personal record.
- Keep playbooks concise (3–5 steps) so SRE/solutions team can reuse quickly.

Quick links / references used while hacking here:
- INF-2981: trace-level counters request (linked above)
- Confluence leverboard-playbook (draft)
- GH PR for batching infra: /pull/462 (perf harness)

Commitment for next week (2026-03-08 to 2026-03-14):
- Ship cache tracing counter and collect 7 days of hits.
- Finish draft TTL policy (session anchor + jitter); run against 1 week of logs.
- Kick off expanded quantization eval set design with research.

Random personal meta:
- Keep this doc lean — copy sections into a team-facing RFC when we have a clear cost/latency story.
- If the cache saves >8% cost in the next 30 days, escalate to product for a small canary rollout.

End of log.
